chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Peanuts's tone and his death (second version)
summary: Peanuts played like mad but had no tone; Mosley saw him in Sweden before he died.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: He was in the band then. And Stuff.
Yes. There's only one thing, he never had a good tone.
He didn't have a good tone; he played like hell.
But he didn't have a good tone; I know he didn't have a good tone.
I wondered why--he was powerful in the band (inaudible). We wouldn't have had him take that lead.
He played a hell of a trumpet in that days.

They did. He was a little, short guy; he was always sensitive about being short and he wore real high heeled shoes. It looked like he was going to tip over on us. I saw him in Sweden; that was some reunion.
He died not so many months after I saw him. He was a little disgusted; he said I can't understand why God lets me stay on earth and I can't play my horn.
I know, but he was still disgusted. He had something in the back of his head; I don't know what it was but he said that one of the doctors said that one of these days it was going to kill him.
